---
title: "Posterior membership"
execute:
  cache: false
---

A Gaussian mixture assigns density to every observed acoustic vector. We now ask how the weighted component contributions divide for one Peterson-Barney token. The [**posterior probability of component membership**](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/mixture.html), often expressed as [**responsibilities**](https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat505/Lesson14), applies Bayes' rule inside the fitted mixture.

## Loading and fitting the fixed mixture

```{r}
source_environment <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
utils::data("pb52", package = "phonTools", envir = source_environment)
pb52 <- source_environment$pb52
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(mclust))

stopifnot(
  identical(dim(pb52), c(1520L, 9L)),
  length(unique(pb52$speaker)) == 76L,
  all(table(pb52$speaker) == 20L)
)

vowels <- pb52 |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    row_id = dplyr::row_number(),
    token_id = sprintf(
      "speaker-%02d-%s-repetition-%d", speaker, vowel, repetition
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(speaker) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    z_f1 = (f1 - mean(f1)) / stats::sd(f1),
    z_f2 = (f2 - mean(f2)) / stats::sd(f2)
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

X <- as.matrix(vowels[, c("z_f1", "z_f2")])
set.seed(1952L)
fit_g10 <- mclust::Mclust(
  X,
  G = 10L,
  modelNames = "EVI",
  verbose = FALSE
)
stopifnot(fit_g10$G == 10L, fit_g10$modelName == "EVI")
```

The intended-vowel column is retained in `vowels` but is not passed to `Mclust()`.

## Conditioning on an unobserved component

Let

$$
Z_i\in\{1,\ldots,K\}
$$

be the unobserved component label. Before observing $\mathbf{x}_i$,

$$
\mathbb{P}(Z_i=k)=\pi_k.
$$

Conditional on component $k$,

$$
f(\mathbf{x}_i\mid Z_i=k)
=
\mathcal{N}
(\mathbf{x}_i;\boldsymbol{\mu}_k,\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_k).
$$

Bayes' rule gives

$$
\mathbb{P}(Z_i=k\mid\mathbf{x}_i)
=
\frac{
\mathbb{P}(Z_i=k)f(\mathbf{x}_i\mid Z_i=k)
}{
f(\mathbf{x}_i)
}.
$$

Substituting the mixture density yields

$$
r_{ik}
=
\mathbb{P}(Z_i=k\mid\mathbf{x}_i)
=
\frac{
\pi_k\mathcal{N}
(\mathbf{x}_i;\boldsymbol{\mu}_k,\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_k)
}{
\sum_{j=1}^{K}
\pi_j\mathcal{N}
(\mathbf{x}_i;\boldsymbol{\mu}_j,\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j)
}.
$$

The denominator normalizes the weighted contributions, so

$$
\sum_{k=1}^{K}r_{ik}=1.
$$

## Calculating every responsibility directly

```{r}
conditional_density <- mclust::cdens(
  X,
  modelName = fit_g10$modelName,
  parameters = fit_g10$parameters
)
weighted_density <- sweep(
  conditional_density,
  2,
  fit_g10$parameters$pro,
  "*"
)
mixture_density <- rowSums(weighted_density)
responsibility <- sweep(weighted_density, 1, mixture_density, "/")

package_estep <- mclust::estep(
  X,
  modelName = fit_g10$modelName,
  parameters = fit_g10$parameters
)

stopifnot(
  max(abs(rowSums(responsibility) - 1)) < 1e-10,
  max(abs(responsibility - package_estep$z)) < 1e-10
)

uncertainty <- 1 - apply(responsibility, 1, max)
reference_row <- which.max(uncertainty)
```

The direct calculation agrees with `mclust`'s expectation step to numerical tolerance. We use the observed token with the greatest fitted uncertainty as the worked case.

```{r}
reference_membership <- data.frame(
  row_id = reference_row,
  token_id = vowels$token_id[reference_row],
  component = seq_len(fit_g10$G),
  mixing_weight = fit_g10$parameters$pro,
  conditional_density = conditional_density[reference_row, ],
  weighted_contribution = weighted_density[reference_row, ],
  mixture_density = mixture_density[reference_row],
  posterior_membership = responsibility[reference_row, ]
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(posterior_membership)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(posterior_rank = dplyr::row_number())

knitr::kable(reference_membership, digits = 6)
```

For row `r reference_row`, the three largest responsibilities are `r paste(format(round(reference_membership$posterior_membership[1:3], 3), nsmall = 3), collapse = ", ")`. They sum to `r round(sum(reference_membership$posterior_membership[1:3]), 3)`, while the remaining components receive negligible mass. The hard assignment keeps only component `r reference_membership$component[1]` and discards this overlap.

## Hard assignments and uncertainty

A hard assignment is

$$
\widehat z_i
=
\underset{k}{\operatorname{argmax}}
r_{ik}.
$$

Define fitted uncertainty as

$$
u_i
=
1-\max_k r_{ik}.
$$

This quantity is zero when one component receives all posterior mass and grows as the mass is distributed across competitors. It remains conditional on the fitted mixture.

```{r}
membership_summary <- data.frame(
  mean_uncertainty = mean(uncertainty),
  fraction_above_point_2 = mean(uncertainty > 0.2)
)
knitr::kable(membership_summary, digits = 3)
```

Mean fitted uncertainty is `r round(membership_summary$mean_uncertainty, 3)`, and `r scales::percent(membership_summary$fraction_above_point_2, accuracy = 0.1)` of observed tokens have uncertainty above the declared descriptive threshold.

## Inspecting intended-vowel metadata after fitting

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-alt: "Fitted Gaussian-mixture membership uncertainty for each intended Peterson and Barney vowel, with raw token values and boxplots."

plot_data <- vowels |>
  dplyr::mutate(uncertainty = uncertainty)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  plot_data,
  ggplot2::aes(x = reorder(vowel, uncertainty, stats::median), y = uncertainty)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.62,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    fill = "grey88",
    color = "grey25",
    linewidth = 0.45
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter(
    width = 0.12,
    height = 0,
    alpha = 0.18, # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
    size = 0.45
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Intended vowel (withheld during fitting)",
    y = "Membership uncertainty"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11)
```

The x-axis uses intended-vowel metadata only after every responsibility has been calculated. Differences across labels describe where the fixed F1-F2 mixture is more or less decisive. They do not estimate listener accuracy.

## Component numbers and conditioning

Exchanging all parameters for two components leaves the mixture density unchanged and merely exchanges responsibility columns. This [**label switching**](https://mc-stan.org/docs/stan-users-guide/finite-mixtures.html) means that the integer attached to a component has no stable phonological meaning across separate fits.

Moreover, a responsibility is not the probability that an intended label is correct. It is conditional on the observed F1-F2 vector, fixed component count, `EVI` covariance family, speaker-relative transformation, and estimated parameters. It does not integrate uncertainty about any of those choices.

## Checking the normalized contributions

1. Which weighted contributions produce the three largest memberships for row `r reference_row`?
2. Why does each responsibility row sum to one?
3. What information does the hard component label discard for this token?
4. Why can component numbers change across equivalent fits?
5. Why is membership uncertainty not a measure of intended-vowel correctness?

Posterior membership normalizes observed weighted component densities and retains fitted overlap. The [next page](expectation-maximization.qmd) uses these responsibilities as weights in iterative parameter updates.
